- "Our wounded are in a bad way. Three of the Union's medicines would see them through."  (text, line 67)
- "That'll keep them breathing. Good. You think of others. That's rarer than courage."  (text, line 68)
- "They took my brother's tags when they took him. They keep things like that on their own ground. I'd like them back."  (text, line 69)
- "His. His name, scratched in by hand. Here. He'd want you to have this. It never missed for him."  (text, line 70)
- "One more thing. The unit who lit the first camp. Designation %s. Still walking around."  (text, line 71)
- "There's a unit I'd like to see in the ground. When he's back on the streets, I'll tell you his number."  (text, line 72)
- "Is it done? ...It is. I can feel it. Thank you. I don't think I'll need anything else."  (text, line 73)
- "They're coming into our ground. Now. Clear what you can carry and go."  (text, line 74)
- "They're walking one of ours to the cells. Right now. You can still get to them."  (text, line 75)
- "Supply drop coming in. Guarded, but not well. Go."  (text, line 76)
- "That one. They're with us, they just don't know it yet. Ask them to keep watch."  (text, line 77)
- "Quiet. Too quiet. Rest while you can."  (text, line 78)
- "Clean. Nobody saw you, nobody followed you home. That's how it's done."  (text, line 79)
- "You got it done, and half the city knows your face. Next time, slower."  (text, line 80)
- "We lost that one. Learn why before you try again."  (text, line 81)
- "Nothing to report? Then go and do something worth reporting."  (text, line 82)
- "That's not what I need."  (text, line 83)
- "When the streets run red fast enough, a dozen dead in a few minutes, something comes down out of the sky. Something with wings."  (text, line 84)
- "Do the morning drill, five of you or more, and do it perfectly. Not one mistake. Then look up."  (text, line 85)
- "Kill the city's lights and keep them dead for a quarter of an hour. Somebody starts a party in the dark, and nobody can stop it."  (text, line 86)
- "Six people dancing in a ring, in this city. Imagine it. They say the whole city joins in."  (text, line 87)
- "Set fifteen fires burning at once. Then watch what the city does."  (text, line 88)
- "The master core, the big one from their nexus. Get it to our scientist and let him crack it open. All their screens change."  (text, line 89)
- "When the dead pile up faster than they can be carried off, or the infested hold half the city, the bones get restless."  (text, line 90)
- "Let the weeds take the streets, every crack full, and leave them be. The city starts to dance."  (text, line 91)
- "There's a priest who'd swallow anything holy. Feed him the master core and pray for rain. A lot of rain."  (text, line 92)
- "Keep the city red for three quarters of an hour straight. The crowd starts wanting a show."  (text, line 93)
- "Nothing you haven't heard from me already."  (text, line 94)

## tips that pop up the first time something happens (sv_livingcity_hints.lua)

`gamemodes/livingcity/gamemode/modules/server/sv_livingcity_hints.lua`


> Note for you (not shown in game): first steps, in this order, a few seconds after you arrive

- "Welcome to the city"  (title, line 60)
- "Welcome. The city keeps running even when you're not around. Tips like this one pop up the first time you run into something new. Press {gm_showhelp} for your quick menu: the nine things you'll do most, on the number keys (keys 6 to 8 change depending on what you're looking at). {gm_showteam} is the same for what only your side, rank and job can do. Press {+menu_context} for the full menu: everything you can do, with the guide at the top. You can turn these tips off in its Settings."  (text, line 61)
- "First stop: Civil Intake"  (title, line 62)
- "You've just arrived in the city with no papers, no room and no ration card. Go to Civil Intake to register (an arrow on your screen shows the way): press {+use} on the terminal there and fill in your details. Until you register you can't get rations or Union work, and Civil Protection units will ask for papers you don't have."  (text, line 63)
- "You're registered, and your identity papers are in your pockets ({gm_showspare1}). Next, get a room from Housing Allocation: press {+use} on its terminal, show your papers, pick a housing block, and stay next to the terminal while it searches. Until you have a room, wait near Civil Intake when a curfew starts: you're allowed to be there."  (text, line 65)
- "Your menus"  (title, line 66)
- "{gm_showteam} has what your side, rank and job can do. {gm_showspare1} opens your pockets (eat, drink, make things, give, wear). {gm_showspare2} opens your jobs and quests, your career (rank and the way up) and the factions, as tabs."  (text, line 67)
- "{gm_showspare2} shows your faction (the Factions tab). Zombies don't have pockets."  (text, line 68)
- "You're a citizen"  (title, line 69)
- "Pick a Union job on your job board ({gm_showspare2}) and work shifts to earn credits and Civil Standing. The higher your standing, the more the Commissary will sell you, and at 100 standing you can join Civil Protection."  (text, line 70)
- "You're in the Resistance"  (title, line 71)
- "You start in plain clothes, so Civil Protection units leave you alone unless they see a gun in your hand. To put on your Resistance gear, open {+menu_context} > Resistance > Gear up. Rebel territory is your home base: the quartermaster, the Resistance supply crate and the vegetable pots are there."  (text, line 72)
- "A shackled vortigaunt"  (title, line 73)
- "You belong to the Combine. You work the Union's shifts (job board, {gm_showspare2}), and your collar suppresses your vortessence (your powers). The Resistance can cut your shackles. Once you're free you can heal and attack with your powers, but Civil Protection units will hunt you."  (text, line 74)
- "Your vortessence: {+attack} fires a bolt at whatever you're looking at, and {+attack2} heals whoever is in front of you, or yourself. Outside rebel territory, Civil Protection units go after you as soon as they see you."  (text, line 76)
- "Civil Protection"  (title, line 77)
- "You're Overwatch: the Combine's soldiers, not its police. Your operations are on {gm_showspare2}. When Civil Protection units call for backup, go and help them. In your unit's quick menu ({gm_showteam}), 4 is Call for backup and 6 sends your 10-20 (marks where you are for other units). The Civil Protection Commissary issues your ammunition and grenades ({gm_showspare1} marks the way to it)."  (text, line 78)
- "Your Arrest Baton: {+attack} hits, {+attack2} arrests, {+reload} searches. Your directives (orders) are on {gm_showspare2}. Your unit's quick menu ({gm_showteam}) puts these on the number keys: call for backup, send your 10-20 (where you are), a BOLO (a lookout for someone), your mask's voice lines and the records terminal, plus search and cuff for whoever you're looking at. Everything else is in {+menu_context} > Unit tools. Get supplies at the Civil Protection Commissary ({gm_showspare1} marks the way)."  (text, line 79)
- "Your claws: {+attack} swipes, {+attack2} moans. The infestation zone is your home. You don't need to eat, and you never go down to bleed out: when your health runs out, you die."  (text, line 81)
- "Your tools"  (title, line 82)
- "{+menu_context} > Unit tools has everything, with a note on what each one does: the records terminal (CIDs, violations, loyalty points, BOLOs and requests), your mask's voice lines, and actions for whoever you're looking at: search, cuff and drag (your unit's quick menu, {gm_showteam}, has the ones you use most). You don't queue for rations: your ration, ammunition and grenades are handed out at the Civil Protection Commissary ({gm_showspare1} marks the way)."  (text, line 83)
- "Chat is spoken out loud: only people near you can hear it. In {+menu_context} > Talk you can yell, whisper, describe what you're doing or what's happening around you, or talk out of character (in chat: /y yells, /w whispers, /me and /it describe, // is out of character)."  (text, line 85)
- "Chat is spoken out loud: only people near you can hear it. Start a message with // to talk out of character to everyone."  (text, line 86)
- "Need a hand?"  (title, line 87)
- "To reach the staff, open {+menu_context} > Help > Ask staff for help (or type @ and then your message in chat). Use it for anything out of character: you're stuck, you have a rules question, or someone is breaking the rules."  (text, line 88)
- "From 21:00 to 05:00 it's night: the city goes dark and curfews happen three times as often. {+menu_context} > The city shows the current time."  (text, line 90)
- "It's night. The streets are darker, and most of the living stay indoors."  (text, line 91)
- "When it rains, it washes the blood off the streets (graffiti stays). Clean water comes from the vending machines and the taps; canal water needs boiling at a stove or a fire."  (text, line 93)
- "{+menu_context} > Me > Pose lets you sit, kneel, lie down or lean (move to stand back up). Me > Gesture: wave, salute, bow, nod and more. Me > Put my hands up raises your hands."  (text, line 95)
- "More than one life"  (title, line 96)
- "You can have more than one character in the city. Go to {+menu_context} > Me > My characters to switch between them or make a new one."  (text, line 97)
- "Hunger and thirst"  (title, line 98)
- "Your hunger and thirst go down over time (the bars at the top left; with the quiet HUD, they only appear once they get low). Get rations from the ration dispensers, and water from vending machines and sinks. If either one reaches zero, you start dying."  (text, line 99)
- "Your hunger and thirst go down over time (the bars at the top left; with the quiet HUD, they only appear once they get low). The Resistance's supply crate in rebel territory gives you food; bins, fishing and the vegetable pots help too. If either one reaches zero, you start dying."  (text, line 100)
- "Where to find your numbers"  (title, line 101)
- "This server hides numbers on screen. Your credits and Civil Standing are shown at the top of your pockets ({gm_showspare1}), and your rank and progress on {gm_showspare2}."  (text, line 102)
- "Camera sway"  (title, line 103)
- "The camera sways slightly as you walk and dips when you land. If that bothers you, turn it off in {+menu_context} > Settings > Camera sway (this only changes it for you)."  (text, line 104)

> Note for you (not shown in game): what happens to you

- "You're down"  (title, line 107)
- "You're bleeding out, but you're not dead yet. Anyone can get you back up by pressing {+use} on you. While you're down you can only whisper. If nobody is coming, you can choose {+menu_context} > Me > Give up."  (text, line 108)
- "Back on your feet"  (title, line 109)
- "You're back up, but badly hurt. Heal yourself with a bandage from your pockets ({gm_showspare1}; you can make one from two rags), a medkit, or a medic."  (text, line 110)
- "You're wanted"  (title, line 111)
- "Civil Protection units are coming to arrest you. Stay out of their sight and your wanted level drops over time. Or turn yourself in for half the sentence: walk up to a unit and press {+use} on them (or use {+menu_context} > Me > Give myself up)."  (text, line 112)
- "Civil Protection units can be wanted too. Stay out of sight and your wanted level drops over time, or press {+use} on another unit to turn yourself in."  (text, line 113)
- "Every Civil Protection unit is looking for you"  (title, line 114)
- "Units now have their pistols out. If your wanted level rises again, Overwatch soldiers are sent, and they shoot to kill instead of arresting you. Stay out of every Civil Protection unit's sight for 45 seconds to lower it (it drops faster in rebel territory)."  (text, line 115)
- "Overwatch is coming"  (title, line 116)
- "A squad of Overwatch soldiers is hunting you, and they shoot to kill. Get out of their line of sight and stay hidden. Your wanted level drops twice as fast in rebel territory."  (text, line 117)
- "Stop and search"  (title, line 118)
- "A Civil Protection unit is searching you. Stand still and put your hands up ({gm_showhelp}, then 2: Put my hands up). If you walk away, you'll be wanted for evading inspection. Anything illegal they find is taken from you."  (text, line 119)
- "Your hands are cuffed"  (title, line 120)
- "You can't use anything, and you can only walk. Someone else can uncuff you. If nobody is around, try {+menu_context} > Me > Work at the cuffs to get free; if anyone sees you doing it, they tighten the cuffs."  (text, line 121)
- "Sociostability: marginal"  (title, line 122)
- "The city's alert level has gone up: Civil Protection units will stop and search more people on the street. Keep your papers ready and don't carry anything illegal. The current level is shown at the top of your screen."  (text, line 123)
- "Units now stop 50% more people. The level shows on your mask's display, and officers can change it in {+menu_context} > Unit tools."  (text, line 124)
- "Judgment waiver"  (title, line 125)
- "This is the city's highest alert level: Civil Protection units are allowed to kill whenever they see fit. Get indoors and stay out of sight until it ends."  (text, line 126)
- "You may use lethal force at your own discretion, and units stop twice as many people. It ends when the city calms down, or when an officer ends it."  (text, line 127)
- "Any contraband (illegal items) in your pockets will be found in a search. Your stash at home ({+menu_context} > Getting by) is never searched, but inspection sweeps sometimes raid it."  (text, line 129)
- "Your story"  (title, line 130)
- "You've done enough ordinary jobs that a story of your own can come up on your board ({gm_showspare2}): a quest with choices, marked as your story. It stays posted until you take it."  (text, line 131)
- "Don't run in front of Civil Protection units"  (title, line 132)
- "A Civil Protection unit told you to stop running. Stop within two seconds and nothing more happens. If you keep running, you'll be wanted for fleeing."  (text, line 133)
- "In custody"  (title, line 134)
- "Serve your sentence and you'll be let out at the release point. A friend can give you a lockpick (Give, in their pockets), and you can pick your cell door when no guard is looking, but escaping makes you wanted. If there's a Combine console in your cell, press {+use} on it to fly a city scanner while you wait."  (text, line 135)
- "Your Civil Standing dropped because of your arrest. Community service jobs on your {gm_showspare2} board earn it back, and so does staying out of trouble."  (text, line 137)
- "You're out"  (title, line 138)
- "You escaped, so you're wanted. Get out of sight. Spare clothes or a uniform will disguise you, and forged papers turn you into someone else."  (text, line 139)
- "Get home"  (title, line 140)
- "A Civil Protection unit has caught you outside after curfew. After three warnings you'll be wanted. The arrow on your HUD points to your housing block. A travel permit gets you past one curfew stop."  (text, line 141)
- "In a CP uniform"  (title, line 142)
- "Civil Protection units on the street think you're one of them, for a while. Don't stay near real units, don't commit crimes, and don't let one search you. Most Combine doors will open for you."  (text, line 143)
- "In Resistance gear"  (title, line 144)
- "Resistance fighters think you're one of them, and Civil Protection units will shoot you on sight. If you stand close to a fighter, they may ask you questions you can't answer, and your cover is blown."  (text, line 145)
- "In plain clothes"  (title, line 146)
- "You look like an ordinary citizen. If a Civil Protection unit sees a gun in your hand, your disguise is blown. Never change clothes in front of a unit."  (text, line 147)
- "You look like an ordinary citizen. Useful for undercover work: citizens talk more freely to you, and nobody salutes you."  (text, line 148)
- "Cover blown"  (title, line 149)
- "They've recognised you. Get away, and change clothes somewhere nobody can see you."  (text, line 150)
- "Conduct strike"  (title, line 151)
- "That kill had no roleplay reason behind it. Two strikes sends you to prison, four gets you kicked from the server. Always give people a reason first: a warning, a demand, or a fight they started."  (text, line 152)
- "A new life"  (title, line 153)
- "Death is permanent here: your last character is gone for good. You have a new name and a new face, and nobody knows you. Getting shot puts you down to bleed out before you die, so next time someone may reach you and get you up in time."  (text, line 154)
- "A new rank can unlock new gear, new jobs and more trust. {gm_showspare2} shows what your rank gives you access to."  (text, line 156)
- "A new rank can unlock new gear: grenades are issued from the rank of Metrocop up. {gm_showspare2} shows what your rank gives you access to."  (text, line 157)

Find more materials in bins, by prying junk apart with a crowbar, and on shot-down scanners."  (text, line 411)
- "Your papers"  (title, line 412)

- "Use it from your pockets ({gm_showspare1}) to heal yourself. Used on someone who's down, it gets them back up faster and with more health."  (text, line 415)
- "It counts as contraband until you draw (equip) or load it from your pockets ({gm_showspare1}), and a search will find it. The black market buys it; the Resistance quartermaster pays more."  (text, line 417)

> Note for you (not shown in game): The dealer, for the waypoint (the official lists leave him out, of course).

- "No dealer in the city right now."  (text, line 47)

> Note for you (not shown in game): id = { trust needed, button, words, place to mark (a LC.WaypointPlaces kind), tips it teaches }

- "Any advice for someone like me?"  (text, line 61)
- "Keep your head down, your papers handy, and your mouth shut. The ones who last are the ones nobody remembers."  (text, line 62)
- "What about curfew?"  (text, line 63)
- "When the voice says two minutes, it means one. Be indoors. I've seen what they do to the ones who are late, and so have the walls."  (text, line 64)
- "The flying things?"  (text, line 65)
- "Scanners. They take your picture. Don't stand under them, don't do anything worth photographing, and if one flashes you, walk, don't run."  (text, line 66)
- "Why does everyone walk so slowly?"  (text, line 67)
- "Run in front of a cop and you're a suspect. Walk. Even when your heart's going like a train, walk."  (text, line 68)
- "Where do people find food, really?"  (text, line 69)
- "The bins. Commissary scraps, things people drop. Nobody checks them as often as they should. Here, I'll show you the nearest."  (text, line 70)
- "And water?"  (text, line 71)
- "Sinks, the machines, open water if you're desperate. Boil anything that isn't from a tap, or you'll be coughing for a week."  (text, line 72)
- "Anything else to eat out there?"  (text, line 73)
- "Fish, if you can find a line. Cook what you catch on a stove or a fire barrel. Raw meat will turn your stomach."  (text, line 74)
- "Things the Commissary doesn't sell?"  (text, line 75)
- "There's a man who trades in what you can't buy. Don't tell him I sent you, and don't let a cop see you with him. That way."  (text, line 76)
- "What's a lockpick good for?"  (text, line 77)
- "Doors that aren't yours. Rooms people left in a hurry. Be quick, be quiet, and never in front of a unit."  (text, line 78)
- "Is anyone fighting back?"  (text, line 79)
- "You didn't hear it from me."  (text, line 80)

> Note for you (not shown in game): His troubles: an unmarked quest line (the owner, 10 November: "little hints in his dialogue that you can help remedy and then he likes you more and gives you better advice"). One at a time, in order, he lets the current one slip when you visit; nothing marks it. Offer him something from your pockets and he takes what he needs: he warms to you (+2), thanks you, and the next trouble surfaces. Help with all of them and he has one last thing to tell you, and something to give. id = { what he'll take (item ids; "food" is anything fit to eat), the hint, his thanks }

- "My legs won't take me to the bins any more. Some days I don't eat at all."  (text, line 90)
- "Food. Real food. You don't know what that means to an old man."  (text, line 91)
- "The tap on my floor's been dry a week. Carrying water up those stairs, at my age..."  (text, line 92)
- "Water. Bless you. I'll make it last."  (text, line 93)
- "This cough. Twenty years I've had it. The Commissary wants more for its medicine than I see in a month."  (text, line 94)
- "Medicine? For me? I'll sleep tonight, for the first time in a long while."  (text, line 95)
- "Some young thug took my ration card in the line. I'm too old to work a shift for another."  (text, line 96)
- "A card? You worked for that. I won't forget it. Not ever."  (text, line 97)
- "What I wouldn't give for a smoke. Even the Union's, and those taste of floor sweepings."  (text, line 98)
- "Ah. Now that's a kindness. Sit with me while I have it."  (text, line 99)
- "Sit down, sit down. My knees aren't what they were. What do you want to know?"  (text, line 103)
- "Ah, you again. Good. Not many come back."  (text, line 104)
- "I don't know you. Ask me something simple."  (text, line 105)
- "Hm. Ask me that when I know you better."  (text, line 106)
- "For me? You're a good one. I won't forget it."  (text, line 107)
- "There used to be one. Not in this part of town, not any more."  (text, line 108)
- "Kind of you. But nothing I need, not that."  (text, line 109)
- "You've done more for me than my own family. Here. My old picks. I won't be needing them, and you might. Doors don't stay locked for people who know how."  (text, line 110)
- "Sit a while. The city's quieter when there's someone to share it with."  (text, line 111)

## the Civil Orientation pamphlet (sv_livingcity_pamphlet.lua)

`gamemodes/livingcity/gamemode/modules/server/sv_livingcity_pamphlet.lua`


> Note for you (not shown in game): Written by someone in the Administrator's office: kind on the surface, a threat underneath (the owner, 10 November: "natural english ... as someone working for the administrator wrote it ... a bit harsh with a veneer of being kind"). Its own words, not the clerk's. id = { page title, the page } (the ids are the clerk's topics, so a page teaches the same tips: LC.InfoDeskTopics).

- "WELCOME HOME /  / You were brought here for your own protection, and the city is glad to have you. In return it asks very little: work, do as you're told, and keep your papers on you. This pamphlet explains how. Please read it carefully. "I didn't know" has never helped anyone. /  / The Office of the City Administrator"  (text, line 26)
- "Nobody in this city goes hungry unless they choose to. Every Union shift you finish earns you a ration card, and each card buys one ration at the dispenser. It really is that simple. Your first meal after you arrive is on us. After that, you earn it like everyone else."  (text, line 30)
- "Idleness is bad for you, and worse for the city. Labor Assignment will find you something suitable. Shifts pay credits and Civil Standing, and every one you finish puts a ration card in your hand. Your shifts are on your work board."  (text, line 32)
- "Housing Allocation finds a room for every resident with a job. Every resident with a job, you'll notice. Your room is where you sleep, where you keep your things, and where you will be when curfew starts."  (text, line 34)
- "Your papers"  (text, line 35)
- "You're registered now, which means, as far as the city is concerned, you exist. Keep your identity papers on you at all times, and show them to any Civil Protection officer who asks. They are entitled to ask. Lost papers can be replaced at Civil Intake, for a fee. Try not to lose them."  (text, line 36)
- "The law"  (text, line 37)
- "The laws are posted on the law board for anyone to read, so nobody can say they weren't told. Do what Civil Protection tells you. Don't run when they're nearby: they'll assume the worst, and they're usually right. If you see something, report it. Your neighbours would do the same for you."  (text, line 38)
- "Curfew is for your own safety. You'll hear a warning two minutes before it starts. When it does, go home to your block and stay there until morning. Anyone found outside will be detained, and nobody wants that, least of all you."  (text, line 40)
- "Civil Standing"  (text, line 41)
- "Civil Standing is how the city knows who it can count on. Work, cooperate and report what you see, and it goes up. Break the rules and it goes down. Let it drop below zero and you'll lose your rations until you've earned them back. Climb high enough, and Civil Protection may have a place for you."  (text, line 42)
- "Civil Protection"  (text, line 43)
- "The city looks after those who look after it. Residents with high enough Civil Standing can apply to join Civil Protection from their work board, under Factions. The uniform brings respect, and a sense of purpose. Do think about it."  (text, line 44)

> Note for you (not shown in game): Ravenholm (the owner, 8 November: "reminiscing of the ending to ravenholm: a graveyard with the church but father gregori is glowing red and his voice lines pitch shifted to sound evil, and zombies are rising from the graves ... if a vortigaunt is free it will appear and send out an effect that is a green version of the portal storm effect from ep2 that washes over gregori and shows that he is actually the good guy ... the administrator appears as actually evil and father gregori starts killing the zombies ... and the administrator flies away defeated") The Saviour turned inside out. The dead rise from the graves and come for the dreamers, who have nothing to fight with (it hurts, in the dream); a giant, red Father Grigori rants from the church. When someone is down to 25 health (or after 55 seconds) the dream turns: No freed vortigaunt alive: propaganda wins. She descends, her soldiers kill the dead, and Grigori flees into the sky. ("Saved.") A freed vortigaunt still alive (a Free Vortigaunt player, awake or asleep, or an NPC cut loose from its shackles): a vortigaunt appears (the player themselves, if they're in the dream) and a green storm washes over everything. Grigori's red is gone and his voice is his own; he blasts the dead with his shotgun before they can hurt anyone, while a giant red figure of her shrieks and flies away defeated.

- "An ordinary resident of the city. Keep your head down, carry your papers, collect your rations. Assignments from the Union earn standing."  (description, line 44)

- "Model Citizen"  (name, line 50)
- "The underground. Low ranks pass for ordinary citizens. Fighters wear the lambda openly and are hunted on sight outside rebel territory."  (description, line 55)
- "Combine locks, screens and terminals are your trade. You carry the multitool: hack doors open, hijack city screens, pull data off Combine terminals. It's contraband: a search will take it."  (description, line 69)
- "Moving the cell's cargo is your trade: guns, ammunition and worse, out past the units to drops all over the city. Your board (F4) has smuggling runs on it, better paid than anything a courier carries. A search that finds the cargo finds you."  (description, line 75)
- "Father Grigori"  (name, line 80)
- "Chaplain of the Resistance. A priest who will not let faith die under the Combine. He tends the wounded with his Blessing and preaches the Word aloud. The Combine have declared his faith contraband, so Civil Protection hunts him on sight outside rebel territory."  (description, line 81)
- "Free Vortigaunt"  (name, line 89)
- "A vortigaunt with the shackles off, fighting beside the people who freed it. Its vortessence heals (right click) and strikes (left click). The Combine want it back in chains, and hunt it on sight."  (description, line 90)
